result:
**Round 105 verdict: PASS.** I checked it in a real browser (Playwright with the installed Chromium, a fresh incognito context per test, no credentials), so `browserVerified` and `realVerified` are both `true`. There are no app bugs. One Low documentation error goes back to B.

**The fix works in the browser:**
- **Blocked drag held in place (1280 and 1440):** across 91 mouse moves, the "move blocked" sentence was announced once, then the release sentence once. Round 104 announced 81 times. The status line stayed the same element, with one child, at all 93 checks. The clips didn't overlap and Undo history didn't change.
- **Fade dragged past its limit and held:** while held at the limit, the final fade readout was added once over 30 moves (round 104: 21 times). The 60 different readouts on the way there were each still announced. The fade stopped at 101.352 s and created one history entry; one Ctrl+Z put it back to 0.
- **Fade dragged within its range:** each of the 30 different readouts was announced once, and the final fade matched the last readout (29.599 s).

**Earlier fixes still hold:**
- Pressing Space twice on an empty project, or Enter twice on a library item that failed to load, still announces the message the second time, and no clip is added.
- The status texts for add, Fit, Delete and Undo match the source code. The status line stays one line high.
- No page errors or hydration warnings, no requests to the token, storage, recording or download endpoints, and no `Authorization` headers.
- **Premium access is not bypassed:** without signing in, the header link opens the demo page with its badge, `/studio/middle-east` asks you to sign in, and `/api/studio-token` returns 401. The fake-token check is blocked because the backend isn't available in the cloud.

**My checks of A's work:**
- **Mutations:** I broke the fix in two ways of my own in a scratch copy. The same tests failed as in A's report: SU5 for the provider change; SA6 and SU5 for the reducer change. The unbroken copy passed 13/13.
- **Tests:** the test files tied to this change are the same 69 A listed, and they all pass (1126/1126).
- **Source:** the commit (`3b6178b`), the 3 changed and 4 new files, and all 537 frozen files were unchanged at start and end, and A's file hashes match. The provider change is exactly the 4 allowed edits. The first four UI tests (SU1–SU4) are unchanged, and no `as`, `@ts-` or `any` was added.
- **Doc 092:** the status line (l.4) and the drag problem entry (l.60) now describe round 105.

**For B:**
- **C-R105-01 (Low, doc only):** doc 092 l.16 still says every status text always counts as a new announcement. The diagram at l.32–44, which I read, shows only the Space key case. This contradicts the new rule. It was outside the sections A was allowed to edit, and it doesn't block publishing.
- **Not checked this round** (none were acceptance rows):
  - a real screen reader;
  - whether one extra announcement can slip in right after release (none in my 4 drags);
  - the extra provider render cost while text repeats.

I didn't run the full test suite, typecheck, build, lint, `npm run verify` or the e2e smoke test; the root gate runs those.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop`:
- c-round-105.md
- c-round-105.json
- c-round-105/ (scripts, outputs, screenshots)
